source: Fannie/Freddie UAD 3.6 via Inman, NAR and NAMB

headline: The appraisal form
*just changed*
slides.fig_caption: The new UAD appraisal format, required since *Nov. 2* for Fannie and Freddie loans
slides.sub: A single, dynamic report replaces the legacy forms, with far more property detail.

slides.label: 2027: the new format is *mandatory for every lender*
slides.body: Lenders granted an exception can submit old-format reports through May 19, 2027. The old format retires June 28, 2027.

slides.title: More detail, *less guesswork*
points: Separate *inside and outside* ratings for condition and quality.
What was updated, and *when the work was done*.
The shape of major parts: roof, HVAC, windows, water heater.
Quality judged on design, materials and workmanship.

slides.title: Get *appraisal-ready*
points: Ask the lender which report format *it is ordering*.
Swap "beautifully updated" for *dated specifics* in the MLS.
Keep invoices, permits and warranties *on file*.
Plan for a *longer appraisal* and review timeline.

slides.title: Specifics *matter more now*
slides.body: The new report rewards specifics. Agents who capture what changed, when, and with what paperwork give appraisers facts to work with, and give sellers fewer surprises.
